answer:
A mixture density network predicts weights $\pi_k(x)$, means $\mu_k(x)$, and positive scales $\sigma_k(x)$, giving $p(y|x)=\sum_{k=1}^K\pi_k\mathcal N(y;\mu_k,\sigma_k^2)$. Use softmax weights, positive scale parameterization, and log-sum-exp to minimize negative log likelihood stably. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html) [2](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book2.html)

If two outcomes near -3 and +3 are plausible, an MSE regressor predicts their mean near zero, which may itself be implausible. A mixture can retain both modes; sample from it or report mode-specific probabilities and intervals. Guard against variance collapse, unused components, and label switching. More components increase flexibility but also estimation difficulty. Evaluate held-out likelihood and predictive calibration rather than only error of the mixture mean.
